source: Eltze 1999, J Neural Transm Suppl 56:83-105, PMID 10370904, doi 10.1007/978-3-7091-6360-3_4 (review); Klockgether et al. 1996, Eur J Pharmacol 301(1-3):67-73, PMID 8773448, doi 10.1016/0014-2999(96)00046-5; DrugCentral 2027 NMDA Ki 4.93
note: NO LABEL EXISTS at any agency tried: openFDA 404, AEMPS CIMA empty, the ANSM composition file holds no budipine, Health Canada DPD 0 rows (budipine is marketed in Germany as Parkinsan). So two peer-reviewed sources carry it and they AGREE on NMDA antagonism and on an antimuscarinic action, and DISAGREE on dopamine: Klockgether 1996 found no dopaminergic activity in vivo ('budipine acts by blocking muscarinic and NMDA transmission while facilitation of dopaminergic transmission does not appear to contribute to its in vivo action ... the anti-NMDA action of budipine is more prominent'), while Eltze 1999 calls the primary action 'an indirect dopaminergic effect as shown by facilitation of dopamine (DA) release, inhibition of monoamine oxidase type B (MAO-B) and of DA (re) up-take and stimulation of aromatic L-amino acid decarboxylase (AADC)'. Eltze describes the NMDA action as 'a low-affinity, uncompetitive antagonist with fast kinetics and moderate voltage-dependency at the phencyclidine (PCP) binding site, comparable to that observed with amantadine'; Klockgether measured IC50 36 uM against [3H]TCP binding and 1.1 uM against [3H]QNB. DrugCentral's NMDA Ki 4.93 (about 12 uM), not flagged MOA, AGREES that the affinity is low. ChEMBL and GtoPdb hold nothing The PCP site lies in the channel pore, which GRIN1 and a GRIN2 subunit form together, so the NMDA receptor is treated as a complex KEPT WHOLE over its five v5 subunit nodes with magnitude 1/5. FOR THE OWNER: the repository's one NMDA precedent is dextromethorphan, which enters at GRIN2A alone on ChEMBL's single-gene row (CHEMBL1972) with magnitude 1.0; narrowing budipine the same way is the alternative
